clue.text: Double the revised rate for entertainment

indicators.note: double asks for the next word to be written twice in a row
revised means reworked, so the letters of rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offering entertainment doubles their recently revised fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' writes THE twice; 'revised' rearranges RATE into ATRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays and stage shows are a classic form of public amusement.

clue.text: Take in house useless to a number

parts.note: H is a standard abbreviation for house
useless as worth nothing, nil, the letter O
X is the Roman numeral ten, a number

explanation.surface: A house so useless it is handed over to a number of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in is to fool them with a trick or deception.

clue.text: The restriction of an ancient capital

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition or restriction

explanation.surface: Restrictions imposed by an old capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient capital is Thebes, in Greece or Egypt; the definition is adjectival.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something belonging to Thebes, the ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Pattern of sufficiency once

parts.note: ex means former, once
ample means enough, sufficient

explanation.surface: A model of former abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: A model or specimen to follow is a pattern.

clue.text: Countryman sounds secure

indicators.note: sounds signals a word that is said like another

parts.note: to secure something is to tie it

explanation.surface: A rural man sounds safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand is a fellow national, a countryman, of that land.

clue.text: Considered correct in principle

parts.note: behaviour judged right on moral grounds rather than practical ones

explanation.definitionFit: Conduct thought morally right accords with moral principles.

clue.text: Almost sure to make a turnover

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Being nearly certain of making a turnover in business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges all ten letters of ALMOST and SURE; the turnover is a gymnast's, not a firm's.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-over-heels roll turns the body over completely.

clue.text: The potato's mashed into something which clears up the last of the food!

definitions.text: something which clears up the last of the food!

indicators.note: mashed potatoes are crushed up, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Mashed potato as the final course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental paste cleans away food left on the teeth after eating.

clue.text: Go round a wizard place near Malta

indicators.note: round signals a turnaround of the word beside it

parts.note: the Wizard of Oz gives OZ

explanation.surface: Travelling around a marvellous spot close to Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wizard' looks like British slang for marvellous; it points to Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: The island is Malta's smaller neighbour in the Maltese archipelago.

clue.text: Hurriedly inserts a hyphen

parts.note: a phrase meaning rushes off, read literally as putting in a punctuation stroke

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means rushes, and literally it is adding a short punctuation line.

clue.text: To clothe in underwear

parts.note: a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Dressing someone in their underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A VEST in Britain is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is formally to robe them in official garments.

clue.text: Quiet composer has lines for an Irish Home Rule advocate

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
Thomas Arne, English composer of Rule, Britannia
L is line, LL lines

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken composer writes a few lines for an Irish politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Stewart Parnell led the nineteenth-century Irish campaign for self-government.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Stewart Parnell led the Irish parliamentary party pressing for self-government.

clue.text: Incredible it was once thought

definitions.meaning: read literally, a conviction that is now in the past

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means unbelievable; read literally it is a conviction held in former times.

clue.text: Suitable gear to bring one into line

parts.note: right means suitable, proper
gear is clothing, dress

explanation.surface: The proper outfit makes someone conform.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a parade-ground command for soldiers to align themselves with the marker on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill order makes each soldier align with the rank.

clue.text: In general German product…

indicators.note: in signals letters sitting inside the next words

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, a German manufactured item.
explanation.walkthrough: The run inside 'general German' is ALGER, not LAGER, so the hidden word is printed with two letters swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale bottom-fermented beer is a famous German brew.

clue.text: Recalls some scandal about a super monarch

indicators.note: about signals moving the letters around

parts.note: K is king, a monarch

explanation.surface: Dragging up gossip about a superb king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges A SUPER with K into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge up old misdeeds is to revive and recall them.

clue.text: … affording a turnover that's splendid

indicators.note: turning over the previous answer writes it backwards

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on from the clue before, standing for its answer

explanation.surface: Continuing: the beer, turned over, gives something grand.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 14 down; its answer, written backwards, gives the splendid word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something majestic, fit for royalty, is splendid.

clue.text: A standby for 19 across, say

parts.note: a painter such as Degas relies on a frame to hold his canvas

explanation.definitionFit: A painter's wooden stand holds the canvas while an artist like Degas works.

clue.text: Tale of Turkish commanders in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman commander

explanation.surface: A story of Ottoman officers withdrawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A long heroic narrative is a kind of story.

clue.text: Tom's familiar turning up on board

indicators.note: turning signals the short word beside it read backwards

parts.note: SS, steamship, means on board a ship

explanation.surface: A tomcat's companion turning up on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A tom is a male cat, and the answer is the familiar name for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pet name for a cat; a tom would know it as a friendly form of address.

clue.text: Illustrator of French chatter

parts.note: de is French for of
gas is idle talk

explanation.surface: A French artist known for chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French painter and draughtsman.

clue.text: No way to address a lady

definitions.text: No way to address a lady

parts.words: No way to address a lady
parts.note: the formal salutation for a letter to a man, wrong for a woman

explanation.definitionFit: This formal letter opening is used for men, unsuitable for a woman.

clue.text: Tree work

definitions.meaning: the sorb, a European tree of the rose family

explanation.definitionFit: The sorb is a tree of that name, and labour done for someone is that duty.

clue.text: More crazy than a club row

parts.note: a bat is a club
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: Madder than a fight at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats in the belfry: madder, comparative of a slang word for crazy.

clue.text: Shelter outside the entrance for a willing recipient

indicators.note: outside puts one word around the other

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A shelter outside the gateway for someone who wants to receive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' means by a will, not eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left a bequest in a testament receives it.

clue.text: A supporter has a right to drink it-albeit sour

parts.note: a leg supports a body or table
R is right

explanation.surface: A fan of a political right finds drink sour.
explanation.walkthrough: Alegar is soured ale, malt vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt vinegar is ale gone sour.

clue.text: Room for a food store

parts.note: a pantry-like cupboard or room where provisions are kept

explanation.definitionFit: A cool room or cupboard keeps provisions.

clue.text: Suffered extortion in Yugoslav tourist area

definitions.meaning: was drained of money by someone
a lake resort in former Yugoslavia, now Slovenia

explanation.definitionFit: To be milked of money, and a Slovenian lake resort of the same name.

clue.text: Fire water

definitions.meaning: a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to set on fire; a Scottish brook is a stream of water.

clue.text: Doing bumper business at the car boot sale?

definitions.text: Doing bumper business at the car boot sale?

parts.words: Doing bumper business at the car boot sale?
parts.note: trading well enough to clear all stock, with bumper and boot as car parts

explanation.walkthrough: A car boot sale is a British market where people sell goods from the backs of their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing all stock through brisk trade.

clue.text: Otherwise the girl I ditched

indicators.note: ditched means dropped, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: Elsie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Or else: the girl I dumped.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in other circumstances, alternatively.

clue.text: The German turned to fish as a diversion

indicators.note: turned means round about, so read backwards

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: A German turned into fish as a distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading clue meant to distract is a false trail.
